SHORT_DESCRIPTION: DPSP III: GEOTHERMAL POWER GENERATION PROJECT
PROJECT_TITLE: DPSP III: Geothermal Power Generation Project
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The Geothermal Power Generation Project targets additional renewable energy baseload generation to reduce Indonesia's reliance on coal. The project will provide financing for expanding geothermal power generation.Output 1: Geothermal power plant constructed and commissioned. The project will support GDE in commissioning a 55 MW geothermal power plant at Dieng, Central Java Province and a 55 MW geothermal power plant at Patuha, West Java province.Output 2: Institutional capacity of GDE strengthened. The project will strengthen GDE's capacity to plan for, develop, and operate geothermal power plants, including management of complex technical conditions, multiple coordinated contracts, and environmental risks.Output 3: Community development program enhanced. The project will support enhancement of GDE's Community Development Program through more strategic engagement with the communities and evaluation of programs that can most meaningfully contribute to improved well-being of nearby communities.The Dieng subproject faces technical challenges and high-density of farming activities, the Patuha subproject is nearby to protected forest. As part of ADB's assistance, the project will enhance health, safety, emergency planning, and development programs for nearby communities. The project will ensure that there will be no impairment of high biodiversity value from forest clearing in critical habitat. These activities will serve as an example for how Indonesia's geothermal resource in similar geographic contexts can be developed without detriment to the existing surroundings.The expansion of the two units will contribute to reaching Indonesia's renewable energy targets and contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions in Indonesia and globally. Additional renewable energy supply will also prevent the development of equivalent fossil fired plants to meet growing electricity demand.

Renewable energy becomes increasingly important for the sustainable economic development of Indonesia. Electrification in remote areas can only be achieved in an efficient way, if renewable technologies are used. In addition, the constant economic growth triggers a raising demand in electricity, of which up to 25% is expected to be covered through climate-friendly renewable sources. At the same time, renewable energy projects in Indonesia show a very high failure rate due to the lack of technical support for design, operation and maintenance. Main reason is a shortage of specialists with skills responsive to the labour market needs.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: STRENGHTENING QUALITY INFRASTRUCTURE FOR THE PHOTOVOLTAIC SECTOR INDONESIA
PROJECT_TITLE: Strenghtening Quality Infrastructure for the Photovoltaic Sector Indonesia
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Module objective - Quality assurance in the photovoltaic (PV) sector has been improved in line with international good practices to support new and existing PV systems in Indonesia. Core issue - Quality aspects are not yet consistently taken into account and the necessary quality assurance services are not yet sufficiently provided and used to ensure the quality, safety and longevity of PV systems in Indonesia. Target groups - The target group are users of quality assurance services in the PV sector. Capacity building takes place especially in quality infrastructure institutions. Political partner - Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM). Methodological approach - The project follows a multi-level approach with emphasis on capacity development in quality infrastructure institutions (meso level). Instruments are long-term experts for project management, consultancy by short-term experts regarding processes and technical content as well as procurements of limited scope. Key outputs - 1. Institutions providing quality assurance services have strengthened their capacities to provide services relevant to the PV sector. 2. Decision-makers in relevant institutions are informed about quality infrastructure services and have a better understanding of their relevance. 3. The awareness of quality and quality assurance services has increased among actors in the PV sector.

DONOR_AGENCY: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
SHORT_DESCRIPTION: STRENGTHENING QUALITY INFRASTRUCTURE (QI) FOR THE ENERGY SECTOR
PROJECT_TITLE: Strengthening Quality Infrastructure (QI) for the Energy Sector
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Indonesia has the lowest rate of electrification of all the major economic powers in Asia, placing it behind other rising economies among the ASEAN states (ASEAN = Association of Southeast Asian Nations). As the use of renewable energy - in particular photovoltaics - is now a cost-optimized option in many off-grid settings, solar electricity will be used for many electrification projects. A central precondition for the successful implementation of these political targets is the use of safe, high-quality components and systems for renewable energy that are adapted to international standards. For this to be possible, the national Quality Infrastructure (QI) has to render internationally recognized and demand-oriented services. The national quality infrastructure comprises metrology, standardization and testing, as well as conformity assessment, certification and accreditation. Currently, demand-oriented, recognized services are not provided in the national QI, or are not used effectively - as a result, the potential of photovoltaics is not sufficiently exploited.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: INDONESIA - SUPPORT FOR THE UTILIZATION OF GEOTHERMAL ENERGY
PROJECT_TITLE: Indonesia - Support for the Utilization of Geothermal Energy
LONG_DESCRIPTION: As part of the Energy development cooperation program, the TC measure is intended to contribute to the improved use of geothermal potential in Indonesia and thus promote electrification and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. The relevant state authorities are to be strengthened in the development of smaller, needs-based geothermal projects (<10 MW), which are currently neither in the focus of private developers nor actively funded by the state. The quality and quantity of data on the geothermal resource required for site development, which are provided by the Ministry of Energy and the subordinate Geological Agency, is to be improved in order to minimize the risk of exploration drilling. The project partner is the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources with its relevant departments and the Geological Agency, which is mandated with the preliminary exploration of geothermal sites.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: DANISH ENERGY PARTNERSHIP PROGRAMME III, INDODEPP
PROJECT_TITLE: Danish Energy Partnership Programme III, INDODEPP
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Indonesia being the fourth most populated country in the world and the sixth largest global emitter of greenhouse gases is an essential partner in the dialogue and action on the green transition. This project focuses on institutional capacity development where transformational change for low carbon development can be achieved.Partners in the project have Government mandate (and authority) in the chosen areas of collaboration. They are already trusted partners in Strategic Sector Projects (DK/ID), and the applied government-to-government modality has been verified as being fit-for-purpose.The formulation process for INDODEPP has included series of close consultations with national partners. In the end of the formulation process partner commitment was confirmed by the joint (DK/ID) signing of a Consultation Document summarizing the main targets of INDODEPP.The project is in line with the Danish Government's Climate Act and targets climate change mitigation and SDGs prioritised in Denmark's strategy The World 2030 for development cooperation.Inclusive, sustainable growth - and development is one of the strategic objectives of Denmark's Strategy for Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Action. Economies in transition and emerging economies are considered key players to achieve the global Sustainable Development Goals. The development strategy underlines the importance of providing support for their sustainable development, as they demand expertise, knowledge, technologies and investments to make appropriate strategic choices. Energy is in this regard a priority sector where Denmark has particular knowledge, resources and interests. The strategy also points to the relevance of building strategic partnerships and government-to-government cooperation to promote common agendas such as climate change.
